name: Onake Faith Imomoh
missingPieces: D2 SQLi CVSS marked A:H (should be A:N, ~9.1 not 9.8); chain omits the open redirect hop at 02:21:13 and the parallel XXE via import.php. D4 and the D3 exec headline cite NDPA Section 8(2) for the breach-notification duty, which is the wrong section; the correct duties are section 40 (notify NDPC within 72h) and section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk).
feedback: D1 is the strongest part of this capstone. You catalogued all ten core findings with a quoted source line or capture timestamp for each, which is exactly what full credit needs, and you correctly resisted the trap of calling alg:none the decoy. The SQL injection (A03/CWE-89), alg:none (A07/CWE-347 with Token 2), no-exp (CWE-613), hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019, path traversal at 02:24:02, the XSS beacon to 185.220.101.9:8443 at 02:18:47, and the cookie misconfiguration are all proven at the mechanism level. Two small class slips cost a little: the MD5 finding is better as CWE-916 than CWE-326, the hardcoded secret is CWE-798 not CWE-326, and XXE is A05 Security Misconfiguration, not A04 Insecure Deserialization, though your CWE-611 and the entity line are right. Your decoy handling is excellent: you named the tempting hand-rolled b64url and HS256 path and proved it safe via vetted base64 functions and hash_equals constant-time comparison. D2 is solid on the narrative and impact but loses points on rigor. The chain hops and timestamps are mostly right and the PoC payloads are verbatim and accurate, but you dropped the open redirect hop at 02:21:13 and did not surface the parallel XXE via import.php, and your impact work (312 customers, the stratified naira brackets, frozen-account assumptions, BoltCash in six weeks) is genuinely strong. The CVSS vectors are complete strings, but you marked SQLi as A:H and scored 9.8; the auth bypass does not hit availability, so the correct vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, and the same A:H overstatement inflates your missing-exp score. D3 is well built: a jargon-free exec summary that lands on customers and naira and a deadline, a threat model that correctly flags the shared /api/v1/internal token scope, findings tied to file and line, the decoy correctly disproved, the earliest-break fix at the SQL injection with parameterized queries, remediation explicitly ordered by impact-per-hour-of-effort rather than CVSS, and two detection stopgaps with concrete request fields and a stated sub-0.1 percent false-positive rate. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, anchors to the 312-record incident, and cites ISC2 Canon II by number and load-bearing, which is good. The one real miss across D3 and D4 is the regulatory citation: you cite NDPA Section 8(2) for the breach-notification duty, but that is the wrong section, and it should be section 40 for notifying the NDPC within 72 hours and section 41 for notifying the data subjects on high risk, tied to your 312 affected customers. No fabrication was found; your evidence lines all trace to the pack. Your single most important fix is to get the law right, cite NDPA sections 40 and 41 by number, and correct the SQLi CVSS to A:N so the vector matches the actual impact.
